mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the market prices in lower risk-free rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 5-day returns due to reduced present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate robust consumer demand and labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns through earnings growth momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and UNRATE decline.

mechanism_narrative: In high-employment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), rising non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signal sustained labor demand that boosts consumer spending and corporate margins, generating positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS rises.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) expansion indicates broad-based economic strength that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 95.0 in a 3-month window signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output capacity and causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL > 240.0) and rising FEDFUNDS (> 0.4%) indicate inflationary pressure and tightening, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns through higher real rates and earnings discounting.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 240.0 and FEDFUNDS > 0.4%.

mechanism_narrative: In manufacturing contraction regimes (INDPRO < 95.0), sustained low industrial output reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, generating negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0.
